## Before you start {.study}

- **What you need:** only this page (a phone is fine). The screens show
  Microsoft Access; Access is only on Windows computers, so the tasks use
  the simulators.
- **Time:** about 40 minutes. Work alone, at your own speed.
- **How it works:** read Steps 1–3, try each simulator and answer the
  questions: the page checks each answer at once. Then do the **Tasks to
  submit**.
- **What you submit:** four letters, on the university e-learning
  platform, before lecture 9.

## Key terms {.study}

{{< glossary db-form db-query db-criterion db-report >}}

## Step 1 · A form: one record at a time {.study}

- A **form** shows **one record** of a table at a time, in big boxes.
- It is easy to read, and easy to fill in: **New record**, type, **Save**.
- The record goes into the table behind the form.

::: {.callout-note title="Model · The library's Books table"}
The college library has a table **Books** (BookID, Title, Type, Pages). The
librarian makes a form for it in two clicks, then reads the books one by
one with the arrows.
:::

**In Access, on a computer.** The orange numbers show where to click.

::: {.screens}
![[1]{.step-n} Click the table **Books**. [2]{.step-n} Click **Create**. [3]{.step-n} Click **Form**. The form shows record 1.](images/access-form-1.png)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/form-lab.html" poster="sims/form-lab.png" title="Form Lab: one record at a time" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Forms"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="a query|a chart"}
What shows one record at a time, in big boxes?
:   a form

    Why: A form is for reading and entering one record at a time.

You save a new record in the form. Where does it go?
:   into the table

    Why: The form only shows the table; the data is in the table.
:::
:::

## Step 2 · Queries: a criterion and a sort {.study}

- A **query** shows only the records that you ask for.
- The **criterion** goes in the **Criteria** row: `"Story"`, `>5`.
- The **sort** goes in the **Sort** row: Ascending or Descending.
- Click **Run** (the red !).

::: {.callout-note title="Model · The stories, A to Z"}
The librarian wants only the books of the type Story, sorted by Title. In
Query Design: Criteria `"Story"` under Type, Sort **Ascending** under
Title, then Run: *Desert Rain*, *The Old Bridge*.
:::

**In Access, on a computer.** The orange numbers show where to click.

::: {.screens}
![[1]{.step-n} Type the criterion under **Type**. [2]{.step-n} Choose the sort under **Title**. [3]{.step-n} Click **Run**.](images/access-query-1.png)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/query-lab.html" poster="sims/query-lab.png" title="Query Lab: ask the table a question" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Queries"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Descending|Price < 1"}
Which criterion shows the products of the type Drinks?
:   Type = Drinks

    Why: The criterion chooses the records of one type.

Which sort puts the names from A to Z?
:   Ascending

    Why: Ascending is A to Z, and small to big.
:::
:::

## Step 3 · A report: ready to print {.study}

- A **report** shows the data of a table or a query, ready to print.
- **Create › Report** makes one in one click.
- A report can **group** the records (by Type), **sort** them and show the
  **total** of each group.

::: {.callout-note title="Model · The library report"}
The librarian clicks the table Books, then **Create › Report**: a page with
all the books, their type and their pages, ready to print for the wall.
:::

**In Access, on a computer.** The orange numbers show where to click.

::: {.screens}
![[1]{.step-n} Click the table **Books**. [2]{.step-n} Click **Create**. [3]{.step-n} Click **Report**.](images/access-report-1.png)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/report-lab.html" poster="sims/report-lab.png" title="Report Lab: a report to print" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Reports"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="a form|delete the rows"}
The manager wants the products on paper, grouped by Type, with totals. What do you make?
:   a report

    Why: A report groups, sorts and adds totals, ready to print.

The report must show the cheapest products first in each group. What do you add?
:   a sort by Price

    Why: A sort puts the records of each group in order.
:::
:::

## Tasks to submit {.tasks}

Use the simulators of this page (the Products table of the Sunrise shop).
For each answer, choose A, B or C.

### Task 1 · Two queries

Step 2 shows how.

a) In **Query Lab**, criterion **InStock = Yes**. How many records? **A**
2 · **B** 6 · **C** 8

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}

b) In **Query Lab**, criterion **Type = Bags**, sort **Price,
Ascending**. Which product is first? **A** Bag · **B** Lunch box · **C**
Pen

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}

### Task 2 · A report and a form

Steps 1 and 3 show how.

a) In **Report Lab**, group by Type and show the totals. What is the
total of Paper? **A** 2.00 JD · **B** 4.00 JD · **C** 12.00 JD

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}

b) In **Form Lab**, add the Pencil (Task 2) and save it. How many records
does the table have now? **A** 8 · **B** 9 · **C** 10

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}
